Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

simcompR 0.1.0

First release.

  • Block-diagram models with named and numbered ports, model parameters and editing functions.
  • Compilation into immutable plans: size propagation, direct-feedthrough graph, algebraic loop detection, deterministic execution order and reuse of the structure when only parameters change.
  • Continuous simulation with deSolve, stopping exactly at source breakpoints, sample hits and events.
  • Discrete and multirate execution with exact sample times.
  • Scheduled and zero-crossing events, switch, relay and stop blocks.
  • Optional Newton solution of algebraic loops with residual diagnostics.
  • Hierarchical subsystems with parameter namespaces.
  • State machine blocks.
  • Parameter sweeps and Monte Carlo experiments with fixed seeds.
  • Versioned JSON model files.
  • Fifteen vignettes.

Known limitations

  • Kinks inside memoryless blocks (saturation, dead_zone, abs, compare, lookup) have no crossing function; put an event on the input when the exact time matters.
  • Top-level events can watch a subsystem output but cannot reset a state inside a subsystem; define such events inside the subsystem.
  • Algebraic loops are solved by Newton iteration with a finite-difference Jacobian, started from zero at each evaluation; there is no initial guess argument yet.
  • Signals are real vectors of fixed size; no buses, matrices or variable-size signals. State machines are flat.
  • sim_param() references cannot be combined in arithmetic (write -a with a gain block or a separate parameter).
  • Block parameters whose names are a prefix of an argument of sim_add_block() (model, type, name) or sim_set_params() (plan) are captured by R’s partial matching; avoid names such as n or p.
  • One deSolve::ode() call per segment: fast sample rates over long spans are slow.
  • method = "radau" and method = "iteration" are not supported; zero crossings need lsoda, lsode, lsodes or lsodar.

Roadmap

  • Buses, hierarchical state machines, crossing functions for saturation and similar blocks, loop initial guesses, a benchmarks directory.

  • Graphical diagram editing.

  • Physical (acausal) component libraries and DAE initialization.

  • Integration with modelcompR, controlcompR and z3r.
